items.domain: Impaired driving: alcohol, drugs, implied consent and drowsiness
items.stem: How does the handbook describe alcohol's effect on thinking?

options.text: Alcohol harms judgment so you no longer make good driving decisions or sense the risks you take, reduces overall vision, lets the mind wander so you cannot concentrate, and lowers comprehension so you may not realize what you are doing.
options.rationale: This option restates a different rule, judgment, vision, concentration, understanding, and does not answer the question asked.

options.text: Alcohol is a drug and a depressant that affects the thought process and does not give a lift, and the decisions made after drinking may well be faulty.
options.rationale: Option B is correct: this is the accepted handbook rule on alcohol is a depressant.

options.text: Alcohol suppresses the senses so you do not feel speed and may speed without knowing it, and it lengthens reaction time so moving the foot from gas to brake takes longer, which can be the difference between arriving safely or not at all.
options.rationale: This option restates a different rule, senses and reaction time, and does not answer the question asked.

options.text: Time is the only way to reduce the effects of alcohol, coffee, a cold shower or running around will not sober anyone up, and the body needs at least an hour per drink to process the alcohol, so several hours may pass before driving is safe.
options.rationale: This option restates a different rule, only time sobers, and does not answer the question asked.

items.correct_rationale: Option B is correct: the handbook rule on alcohol is a depressant answers the question, and the other options restate different rules.

options.text: Avoid driving when drowsy, and if drowsiness strikes on the road find a safe place to pull over and stop, because opening the window or turning up the radio will not keep you awake and looking for ways to stay awake is itself the sign to stop and rest.
options.rationale: This option restates a different rule, pull over when drowsy, and does not answer the question asked.

options.text: Many crashes each year happen because a driver falls asleep at the wheel, often ending in a head on crash with another vehicle, a tree or a roadside object, and drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they appear drunk.
options.rationale: This option restates a different rule, falling asleep at the wheel, and does not answer the question asked.

options.text: The Vermont Emergency Nurses Association sponsors signs at the sites of alcohol related fatal crashes, and each sign marks a place where someone died because of a drunk driver.
options.rationale: This option restates a different rule, signs at fatal crash sites, and does not answer the question asked.

items.correct_rationale: Option A is correct: the handbook rule on drowsy versus drunk, and the remedy answers the question, and the other options restate different rules.

items.domain: Impaired driving: alcohol, drugs, implied consent and drowsiness
items.stem: Besides alcohol, what else can impair a driver?

options.text: Impairment is not limited to alcohol: drugs, including prescription and over the counter medicines, can seriously affect driving, and drowsy driving is also dangerous.
options.rationale: Option A is correct: this is the accepted handbook rule on three sources of impairment.

options.text: Driving after taking other drugs or narcotics, even prescription or over the counter ones, can be as deadly as alcohol or deadlier for some people, since drugs can cause sleepiness and poor thinking, and time is again the only remedy.
options.rationale: This option restates a different rule, other drugs can be deadly too, and does not answer the question asked.

options.text: If you plan to drink, plan first: use a designated driver who agrees not to drink or use drugs and takes responsibility for getting everyone home, or call a parent or other responsible person for a safe ride.
options.rationale: This option restates a different rule, plan before you drink, and does not answer the question asked.

options.text: Other safe plans are to stay overnight where you are if it is safe, to take friends seriously when they warn you not to drive, and to hand your keys before drinking to a non drinking friend who will not let you drive.
options.rationale: This option restates a different rule, more safe ride plans, and does not answer the question asked.
